institutionName: Institut d'Etudes Politiques de Toulouse (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my French, but also to experience Toulouse

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That I could take my courses in French and that the place was nice

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was nice to have my courses in French, I got new friends and I likes my appartement and my roomies. It was a bit sad though that I wasn't in the same class as the French students.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: In generel I found it quite difficult to get the information I needed, but everything turned out well. It was stressful though, so I hope for future students that they will get more information/help during the process.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I needed help to get my French E-mail working, and they helped me at the University.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They could help with administative stuff at the University, which was good, but in generel the courses, exams etc. weren't that organized.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was satisfied with an accomodation outside Toulouse, so therefore it was quite easy for me.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In generel it's more expensive, but besides from that I think it's very difficult to say anything in generel. It is possible though to find nice appartments for sharing in the city center that aren't that expensive (maybe 400 euros if you are lucky). Normally I would say the price is more around 500-600, if you want to find something in the center.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the registration part was easy but all the stuff relating to the registration was difficult and confusing, for example knowing how to get you ETCS approved

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think I just sent a letter and then my home University did the rest. But to be honest I don't really remember...

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could write my home University or my host University. My home University was extremely slow in answering, so in practice they weren't that helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was diffucult to know how to get my ECTS and how much information my home University needed. Once in Toulouse, it was very easy to register.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's so easy. Or at least it was for the students at this fall semester, because we had our classes seperately from the French students, so I can't relly give any advice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it wasn't really difficult, but I was still challenged.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the academic level of the courses lower than at my home University. In a way it was nice though due to the challenge of the French language. Also, I had twice as many courses than I normally have at my home University, so maybe that also explaines why each course was easier than a course at my home University.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some teachers used Powerpoints (just like my professors at my home University) which was a great help in understaning the points and the language. Other teachers only read out loud from a paper, which was very boring and which made it difficult to understand the content.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Les Institutions européens, Sociologies des partis politiques, Humanités numériques, Introduction aux relations internationales, Introduction au Droit public, Economie régionale et urbaine, Stage introductif de Francais Langue Etrangère, Francais et méthodologie, cultures et civilisation francaises,

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Humanités numériques, Introduction aux relations internationales, Introduction au Droit public,

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and public transportation was less expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of sports clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joinded the dance club of the University, which was nice and also a way to get to know some French people. If you like board games then you should go to "Les Tricheurs"!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to other cities like Albi, Carcassonne, Bordeaux.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a sports club.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Join a sports club if you want to meet French people. But also just talk with French people at the night clubs. Work hard, but don't get stressed - the teachers are nice. And enjoy!!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I've heard the the students recidences aren't that social, so if you want to live in a "social" accomodation I think the best you can do is to find a shares appartement, but then again, you never know who you are going to live with so it's always a bit of a gamble. Use the cantine!! It's very cheap.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I improved my French (even though the Erasmus test doesn¨t show it I know that I did). And then I met a lot of nive people and got the experience the Southern France.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be away from the people I love in Denmark

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
